name: Example: Calculating Components of Acceleration at a Particular Moment
problem: The position $\mathbf r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)= \langle e^{2t}, \, e^{-t} , \, 1 \rangle,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t = 0\,\textrm s.$
worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t = 0,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{2t},\,-{e}^{-t},\,0⟩, \\ v(0) & =⟨2{e}^{2(0)},\,-{e}^{-0},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t = 0{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{e}^{2t},\,{e}^{-t},\,0,⟩ \\ a(0) & =⟨4{e}^{2(0)},\,{e}^{-0},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\mathbf v(0) \cdot \mathbf a(0)$ and $||\mathbf v(0)||\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0)\cdot a(0) & =⟨2,\,-1,\,0⟩\cdot ⟨4,\,1,\,0⟩ \\  & =7, \\ ||v(0)|| & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=0,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(0)\cdot a(0)}{||v(0)||} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $\dfrac{7\sqrt{5}}{5} \, \textrm{ms}^{-2}.$
